captions.instagram:
"Get an LLC for the taxes" is advice artists hear a lot. What a one-owner LLC actually does:

✔️ By default the IRS disregards it for income tax. You still file Schedule C with your Form 1040.
✔️ Self-employment tax still applies to your net earnings.
✔️ It is a separate legal entity under state law, which is why people form one.
✔️ An LLC can elect S corp status (Form 2553). Then you pay yourself a reasonable salary through payroll, with payroll taxes and extra costs, so it's usually worth a look only at higher profit.

Thinking about forming one? We form LLCs in all 50 states. Our artists page has the details.

sources.fact: An LLC is an entity created by state statute; a one-member LLC is treated as disregarded from its owner for income tax unless it elects corporate treatment (Form 8832) (read 2026-10-25)

Individual-owned single-member LLC reports income and expenses on Schedule C and the owner is subject to self-employment tax; an LLC files Form 2553 to elect S corporation classification (Pub 3402, read 2026-10-25)
S corporations must pay reasonable compensation to a shareholder-employee for services; those payments are wages subject to employment taxes (read 2026-10-25)
